One source of vivid, irrefutable evidence of vehicular use destruction can still be seen in many of the early pioneer emigrant trails which crisscrossed the Creat Basin during the early and mid-1800's. The Oregon Trail, for instance, has not seen use since its abandonment in 1872—yet, in many areas the trail ruts are still there, with their complement of exotic infesting plants, a century after vehicular use(in this instance, by covered wagons) ceased. The same destructive effects can be directly attributed to ORV use on defacto roadless public lands. One far-reaching form of remedial action proposed by NORA has been the selective designation of existing remote and back country primitive, jeep and macadam roads and trails (excluding, in the latter case, those lands deemed suitable for wilderness and natural area preservation) as part of a system of Adventure Roads. Since 1958, when NORA began its pioneer effort to seek out and identify scenic, unique-natural, wilderness, and recreational sites and arcss (which now numbers mearly 450 in Nevada alone), we have included in our program a comprehensive inventory of roads and trails which would be cuitable for this Adventure Roads program on our public lands. Where we observed such roads and trails in exceptional open space conditions, we included—and are presently still developing—a district by district plan for open space receives.
